payload.headline: AMD falls 8.86% to 413.27, still well above every fair-value estimate

summary.thesis: The business is growing fast and margins are rising, but the price still needs much faster cash-flow growth than the valuation model allows.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no trade while the stock is in a downtrend and below its 200-day average.
summary.act_at: Long-term at 333.38 or lower; swing only after a close above 451.0

payload.happening: AMD closed at 413.27, down 8.86% in one day. That erased yesterday's rebound and put the price below its 200-day average of 432.0. DATA lists no news since the last note, so nothing here explains the drop. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
payload.business: The business numbers did not change today. The latest filing (2026-11-04) shows quarterly sales up 44.68% from a year earlier, faster than the 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after investment) is 7.1B over the last twelve months, up from 5.4B, and the company holds 8.7B more cash than debt. Analysts raised next-year EPS estimates by 11.3% in the last 30 days. Demand, margins and cash all look solid. The business risk sits in two places. Inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. The 18% operating margin is also near the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. Today's fall reflects sentiment: the technical and macro readings in DATA describe a tech market in a downtrend with elevated fear. None of this changes the company's cash or its competitive position.

worth.text: At 413.27 AMD trades at 90.1 times trailing earnings, 51.1 times this year's expected earnings and 23.4 times next year's. It is 14.9 times sales, against a peer median of 13.3, and its own 5-year price-to-sales sits in the 88th percentile. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values future cash) gives 145.29 to 220.22, with 186.22 in the middle. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. To justify the price, the model needs free cash flow to start growing about 52.3% a year, but it caps starting growth at 30%, which gives about 189.77. That cap explains most of the gap. The price can hold only if analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth turns into lasting cash-flow growth. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 13%, the value drops to 100.01.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 52.3% a year, but the model caps it at 30%, so the gap depends on analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth lasting.

bull: Sales are accelerating: quarterly revenue grew 44.68% year over year, up from 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability is improving fast: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow reached 7.1B.
Analysts are turning more optimistic: next-year EPS is 17.64, up 11.3% in 30 days, which puts the stock at 23.4 times next year's earnings.
bear: The price implies 52.3% starting cash-flow growth, well above the model's 30% cap, and every valuation method tops out at 333.38.
Inventory grew 57% while sales grew 45%, which can lead to price cuts. If operating margin fell to 13%, the value drops to 100.01.
Price-to-sales is 14.9, above the peer median of 13.3 and in the 88th percentile of AMD's own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 391.88–403.58 support zone. A close below it would mean the selloff is deepening, though the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range. The value case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is strong, but the price needs 52.3% cash-flow growth to make sense. Wait for 333.38 or lower, or for results that support much faster growth.

swing.why: The trend is down: price is below the 20-day (497.84), 50-day (550.48) and 200-day (432.0) averages, with lower highs and lower lows. The average daily range (ATR) is 46.79, wider than the gap to the 391.88–403.58 support, so a stop there would sit inside normal daily noise. No trade until a close above 451.0, the top of the 424.03–451.0 resistance.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are more than two months away. Options price a 17.4% move by 2026-12-18, puts outnumber calls 1.78 to 1 in open interest, and the most put interest sits at the 400 strike, so sentiment alone could push the price through the support zone before the report.

change_mind: A close at or below 333.38, the top of the fair-value range, would open the long-term value case.
At the 2027-02-02 report: inventory growing slower than sales, with operating margin holding near 17.72%, would ease the main business risk.
A close above 451.0, out of the 424.03–451.0 resistance zone, would end the swing no-trade stance. A close below 391.88 would confirm a deeper selloff.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, confirmed by the 8.86% drop to 413.27, which leaves the price above the 333.38 top of the fair-value range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
